alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C (wt%). Measured composition (Table 1, wt%): C 0.97, Mn 27.91, Al 8.04, S 0.004, P 0.006, Fe Bal. Single-phase austenitic (FCC) structure; no deformation-induced martensitic transformation reported during CR.
alloys.description: Low-density experimental Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) austenitic steel ('test steel'), produced by vacuum melting and casting; the ingot was heated to 1200°C for 2 h and hot forged into billets. Density 6.82 g cm^-3.

source.reason: The paper studies a single low-density steel with nominal composition Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C (in wt%), explicitly referred to as 'test steel'; the detailed chemical composition is given in Table 1.

paper.paper_scope: Systematic experimental investigation of the influence of cryogenic rolling (CR) deformation (30%, 50%, 70%, 90% thickness reduction) on the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of low-density Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C austenitic steel.
paper.title: Effects of Cryogenic Rolling on the Microstructure Evolution and Mechanical Properties of Low-Density Fe-28Mn-8Al-1C Steel

processes.description: Plate specimens solution treated at 1000°C for 1 h and water-quenched to room temperature; no cryogenic rolling applied (reference/undeformed state).
processes.process_name: Solution treatment at 1000°C for 1 h + water quench
processes.processes_notes: Reference state before any CR deformation; exhibits equiaxed austenite grains (~40.3 μm).

source.reason: Before CR, all specimens underwent solution treatment at 1000°C for 1 h and were water-quenched to room temperature; this undeformed state is used as the reference for microstructure and mechanical property comparisons.

processes.description: After solution treatment (1000°C/1 h + WQ), specimens immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3-5 min and rolled about 2% per pass, repeated to a cumulative thickness reduction of 30%.

source.reason: Test steels were cryogenic rolled (liquid nitrogen immersion 3-5 min, ~2% per pass) to cumulative thickness reductions including 30%; this state is reported for microstructure evolution.

processes.description: After solution treatment (1000°C/1 h + WQ), specimens immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3-5 min and rolled about 2% per pass, repeated to a cumulative thickness reduction of 50%.

source.reason: Test steels were cryogenic rolled to cumulative thickness reductions including 50%; this state is characterized by dislocation entanglement, walls and deformation twins.

processes.description: After solution treatment (1000°C/1 h + WQ), specimens immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3-5 min and rolled about 2% per pass, repeated to a cumulative thickness reduction of 70%.

source.reason: Test steels were cryogenic rolled to cumulative thickness reductions including 70%; this state shows larger dislocation cells and decreasing twin density.

processes.description: After solution treatment (1000°C/1 h + WQ), specimens immersed in liquid nitrogen for 3-5 min and rolled about 2% per pass, repeated to a cumulative thickness reduction of 90%.

source.reason: Test steels were cryogenic rolled to cumulative thickness reductions including 90%; this state yields fibrous nanoscale grains (avg 58.8 nm) and the highest strength.
Undeformed test steel (solution-treated at 1000°C/1 h and water-quenched) is characterized as the reference state, with equiaxed grains of ~40.3 μm.
Test steel after 30% CR reduction; equiaxed grains elongate along RD with slip bands and Taylor lattice structure.
Test steel after 50% CR reduction; shows flattened/banded grains, dislocation entanglement and walls, and deformation twins.
Test steel after 70% CR reduction; larger dislocation cells form with increasing dislocation density while twin density decreases.
Test steel after 90% CR reduction; fibrous nanoscale grains (avg 58.8 nm) with the highest UTS/YS/microhardness and lowest elongation.
